was: RV resort on a 2,000-acre nature development off Hwy 105 near Cleveland; full-hookup 30/50-amp sites with an instant-book nightly rate (~$45) offered alongside RV-homesite lot sales; multiple on-site fishing lakes, sandy-beach swim areas, and trails. Reservable online (RoverPass). --Claude
note: Nature-focused land development at 201 Cypress Lakes Circle, Cleveland, about an hour from Houston or Beaumont, behind a gated entrance: 2,000 acres with five fishing lakes, 1.2 miles of sandy beach, pools, a splash pad, an equestrian center, trails and a dog park.  Nightly guests get full-hookup 30- or 50-amp RV pads, booked on RoverPass for at least 2 nights and checked in at the sales office; tents, toy haulers, truck campers and pop-ups are not allowed.  The development also sells homes, cabins, lots and RV pads with owner financing. --Claude

was: Spread-out high-desert RV/glamping park on 90 acres at Terlingua Ranch (Sombrero Peak Rd), near Big Bend NP; pull-through sites handle up to 42-ft rigs, power pedestal + community water fill + dump station, no sewer/no cell service, dark-sky stargazing. Reachable via graded desert dirt roads. Reservable online (RoverPass). --Claude
note: Remote high-desert park at 889 Sombrero Peak on Terlingua Ranch, 35 miles north of Terlingua, its owner living on site: pull-through sites of about a quarter acre with electric hookups, for rigs up to 42 ft. was: Island County Fairgrounds campground in Langley, operated by the Port of South Whidbey (port district); a real year-round campground open to transient overnighters (closed only during the fair) with 50 sites incl 40 RV hookup sites, dump station, restrooms/showers, 14-day limit, FCFS.
